stem: You want to compare the effect of several different error-mitigation settings on one circuit and observable. The jobs are independent, all known at the outset, and you want them to run as closely together in time as possible (to limit device drift) while still being able to inspect each job's result separately. Which execution mode does the documentation recommend?

options.text: Job mode, submitting all jobs and hoping the scheduler groups them
Session mode, which generally keeps the jobs closest together in time.
A separate session per mitigation setting
Job mode with one job that carries every mitigation setting as a separate PUB, so one queue wait covers all of them.
One primitive job per setting, submitted from several parallel Python processes so they generally reach the QPU at the same moment.

explanation.correct: All jobs are independent and available at the outset, so they can be scheduled collectively in a batch: you wait through the queue only once, the classical pre-processing runs in parallel, and the jobs run closely together to limit drift, while you still get each job's result individually. Because sessions are generally more expensive, batch is preferred whenever dedicated access is not required.

distractors.A: Plain job mode creates no scheduling relationship between jobs — each waits in the queue separately with no guarantee they run close together.
distractors.B: A session does keep jobs tightly together, but it is generally more expensive; the docs recommend batch whenever you do not need a session's dedicated access.
distractors.D: Opening a session per setting multiplies session overhead and cost while giving independent jobs no benefit.
distractors.E: Primitive options — including the error-mitigation settings — are set on the primitive and apply to the whole job, not per PUB. One job cannot carry several different mitigation configurations, and a single job also returns one result object rather than separately inspectable per-setting results.
distractors.F: Submitting in parallel does not make jobs run together: each one still enters the fair-share queue independently and they can be separated by hours. Batch is the mechanism that asks the scheduler to treat a group as a unit.

provenance.notes: meta-pattern fix pass: length/stem-echo/absolute calibration (s4) — hedged + lengthened the session distractor (absolute-tell fix). | pool wave: +E (options are per-PUB), +F (parallel submission substitutes for batching)
